decisions.reason: Audio and web conferencing is a low-investment add-on with only passing mention, so dropping it would cost little, but it still fits the integrated communications offer and has no clear failure signal yet.

The metro data centre network rests on heavy owned fibre investment, has a publicly cited customer adoption, and is central to the announced high-bandwidth direction, so management will persist with it.
Optical spectrum is featured on its own page and builds on costly fibre assets central to the firm's high-bandwidth strategy, so visible commitment and sunk investment favour keeping it.
The number ordering portal is a cheap software layer on the established voice platform that supports the real-time provisioning direction, so there is little reason to withdraw it.

Carrier pre-selection is a declining legacy telephony service with little investment or public commitment behind it, and its weakness reflects structural market decline rather than temporary causes, so dropping it costs little.
Direct voice network connection stays close to the core voice business and fits the cloud voice transition, so it is likely retained.
